component.name: Apache Superset
component.description: Data exploration and visualization platform. The security model is written in terms of principals, trust boundaries, and capability surface rather than specific files or libraries, so new code paths inherit the model automatically. The in-scope test is a single question: does the finding let a principal perform an action the role and capability matrix does not entitle them to?

externalReferences.comment: Source security model document (SECURITY.md); this file is a structured translation of it.

blueprints.name: Superset trust boundaries and principals
blueprints.description: The security model assumes three trust boundaries: the Admin role (fully trusted operational principal, by policy equivalent to operating-system-level trust over the application), the operator (whoever deploys, configures, and runs Superset; deployment-time decisions are theirs), and the Superset codebase (responsible for enforcing the role and capability matrix across its product surface).

assets.name: Apache Superset codebase
assets.description: Responsible for enforcing the role and capability matrix across its product surface, and for controls its own documentation explicitly positions as security boundaries (row-level security, access checks tied to the matrix). A failure to enforce, anywhere in that surface, is in scope.

assets.name: Trusted backend infrastructure
assets.description: Metastore, cache backends (for example Redis or Memcached), message brokers, secret stores, and other operator-managed infrastructure whose integrity Superset assumes.

zones.name: UI and API principals
zones.description: Public (anonymous), Gamma, Alpha, Admin, and embedded guest token principals interacting through the documented user interface and REST API.

zones.name: Superset application
zones.description: The Superset codebase enforcing the role and capability matrix.

zones.name: Operator-managed backend infrastructure
zones.description: Metastore, caches, brokers, and secret stores assumed to have integrity; findings requiring tampering with them are post-compromise scenarios.

persona.description: Fully trusted operational principal. Anything an Admin can do through the documented UI, REST API, or configuration system is an intended capability, not a vulnerability: registering database connections of arbitrary type, executing arbitrary SQL through SQL Lab, rendering Jinja templates resolving to SQL or HTML, overriding configuration. Granting Admin is functionally equivalent to granting shell access on the host (MITRE CNA Operational Rules 4.1 reasoning). Has all capabilities: read all data, write all objects, execute SQL, manage databases, manage users, roles, and RLS.

Whoever deploys, configures, and runs Superset. Responsible for deployment-time decisions: values of secrets, network reachability of the application and its data sources, choice of database connectors and cache backends, feature flags, notification destinations, and trust placed in third-party plugins.

Reads all data sources; writes own charts, dashboards, and datasets; no SQL execution by default (requires the additive sql_lab role); may upload data to existing databases only; cannot manage users, roles, or RLS.
Reads only granted datasets; writes own charts and dashboards on granted datasets; no SQL execution by default (requires the additive sql_lab role); no database or user management.

No data access by default. Operators may grant the Public role read access to specific datasets or dashboards (typically for anonymous reporting), which shifts the boundary for that deployment without redefining the model.
May read only data sources reachable through the embedded dashboards the token authorizes; no writes, SQL execution, database management, or user management.

assumptions.description: Superset assumes the integrity of its metastore, cache backends, message brokers, secret stores, and other operator-managed infrastructure.

Deployments may grant or revoke individual view-menu permissions, which shifts the boundary for that deployment but does not redefine the model; custom roles have whatever capabilities the operator explicitly granted.

The sql_lab role is additive: it grants the SQL Lab permission set on top of the base role and is the only path by which Gamma or Alpha gain SQL execution capability; database access remains scoped per the base role's grants.

threats.name: Principal acts outside the role and capability matrix
threats.description: A user, embedded guest, or anonymous visitor reads, modifies, or deletes data outside their granted set, including object-level access bypass on charts, dashboards, datasets, saved queries, tags, annotations, and similar per-object endpoints; row-level-security rule bypass; reaching a route, page, or API endpoint requiring a role they do not have; or bypassing any control Superset documents specifically as a security boundary.

threats.name: Injection of SQL, template code, or scripts
threats.description: A user supplies input that the codebase should sanitize or parameterize but does not, causing arbitrary SQL, template code, or scripts to execute. Includes injection through Jinja templates, SQL-construction paths, and any field the codebase passes to a query engine or template engine.

threats.name: Authentication bypass or session attacks
threats.description: A user bypasses authentication, fixates or reuses another user's session, or reaches an authenticated endpoint without logging in.

threats.name: Embedded guest token forgery, replay, or escalation
threats.description: An embedded guest token authorizes actions outside the dashboard it was issued for, or can be forged, replayed, or escalated to a higher principal.

threats.name: Server-side request forgery
threats.description: Superset, acting on behalf of an unprivileged user, fetches an outbound URL the user controls in a feature where Superset itself, not the operator, controls the outbound destination set.

threats.name: Cross-site scripting and cross-origin leakage
threats.description: A user causes a script to execute in another user's browser through a field the codebase renders to that other user, or causes cross-origin leakage of authenticated session state or data. (Self-XSS affecting only the injecting user is not a qualifying finding under the scope test.)

threats.name: Undocumented fail-open default
threats.description: A Superset default fails open without an accompanying documented hardening requirement. The codebase is responsible for shipping fail-closed defaults or for documenting the hardening required when a default fails open; failures of that responsibility are in scope. Applying documented hardening is the operator's responsibility.

threats.name: Vulnerable pinned direct dependency or vulnerable dependency usage
threats.description: A finding caused by Superset pinning a known-vulnerable version of a direct dependency it ships, or using a dependency in a way that creates a vulnerability the dependency itself does not have, is in scope. By contrast, findings in transitive dependencies or operator-selected dependencies Superset does not ship are out of scope and should be reported to the dependency's maintainers; first-case dependency findings in the official Docker image can be remediated by extending the image at release time.

threats.name: Actions performed by the Admin role
threats.description: Any action an Admin can perform through documented configuration, API, or UI, including arbitrary SQL through SQL Lab, arbitrary database connections, Jinja template rendering, and configuration overrides. The Admin role is a trusted operational principal by policy; per MITRE CNA Operational Rules 4.1, behavior within a documented trust boundary does not violate a security policy.

threats.name: Deployment and operator decisions
threats.description: Behaviors that depend on deployment-time decisions: values of secrets and tokens, whether internal networks are reachable from the server, which database connectors or cache backends are enabled, which feature flags are set, where notifications are delivered, and which third-party plugins are loaded. These are the operator's responsibility, not Superset's.

threats.name: Compromise of trusted backend infrastructure
threats.description: Findings that require an attacker to read from, write to, or tamper with the metastore, cache backends, message brokers, secret stores, or other operator-managed infrastructure, including injecting malicious state, serialized objects, cache entries, task metadata, configuration, or database records. These are post-compromise scenarios, not vulnerabilities in Superset; a finding remains in scope only if an unprivileged user can cause such modification through a vulnerability in Superset itself.

threats.name: Lingering expired key-value or metastore-cache entries
threats.description: The continued presence of expired key-value or metastore-cache entries not yet deleted from the metadata database. Such entries are excluded from reads once expired, purged opportunistically on write, and removed in bulk by the scheduled prune_key_value maintenance task; their lingering until purged is an eventual-cleanup property, not a security boundary.

threats.name: Downstream interpretation of Superset output
threats.description: How a downstream application (spreadsheet program, email client, browser handling user-downloaded files) interprets output Superset produced for it is out of scope.

threats.name: Brute force, rate limiting, and denial of service
threats.description: Brute force, rate limiting, denial of service, or resource exhaustion that does not bypass a documented control is out of scope.

threats.name: Low-impact information disclosure
threats.description: Missing security headers, banner or version disclosure, user or object enumeration through error messages or timing, and similar low-impact information disclosure that does not enable a further concrete exploit.

threats.name: Bypass of undocumented defense-in-depth hardening
threats.description: Bypasses of configurable defense-in-depth hardening Superset does not document as a security boundary. Superset is not a SQL or database firewall: operator-deployable filters such as SQL function or table denylists, URI restrictions on already-authorized database connectors, and similar belt-and-braces controls let operators layer hardening on top of the role and capability matrix, not firewall-grade guarantees. Findings against such hardening are improvements, not vulnerabilities, unless the documentation positions the specific control as security-relevant. Plain hardening suggestions that do not violate the model are likewise out of scope.

trustBoundaries.name: Principal boundary
trustBoundaries.description: Public, Gamma, Alpha, embedded guest token, and Admin principals interact with the codebase through the UI and REST API; the codebase must enforce the role and capability matrix against every principal except Admin, who is trusted by policy.

trustBoundaries.name: Backend infrastructure boundary
trustBoundaries.description: Superset assumes the integrity of its metastore, caches, brokers, and secret stores; tampering with them is a post-compromise scenario outside the model.

controls.name: Role and capability matrix enforcement
controls.description: The codebase enforces the documented capabilities of Public, Gamma, Alpha, Admin, and embedded guest token principals (read data, write objects, execute SQL, manage databases, manage users/roles/RLS) across its product surface; the additive sql_lab role is the only path by which Gamma or Alpha gain SQL execution. Detailed permission definitions live in the Security documentation.

controls.name: Row-level security
controls.description: Row-level security is a control Superset documents specifically as a security boundary; the codebase commits to enforcing it, and bypasses are in scope regardless of which principal triggers them.

controls.name: Fail-closed defaults or documented hardening
controls.description: Defaults that fail closed are the responsibility of the codebase; defaults that fail open must be accompanied by a documented hardening requirement, with applying that hardening being the operator's responsibility.

controls.name: Operator-deployable defense-in-depth filters
controls.description: Operator-deployable belt-and-braces controls (SQL function or table denylists, URI restrictions on already-authorized database connectors, and similar) that let operators layer hardening on top of the role and capability matrix. Not documented as security boundaries.
